text:
alice-support: heads up — customer 'FinData' hit a batch of 401s for our /v1/generate endpoint, started ~10:30 UTC. They say tokens used to work, nothing changed on their side. error from our gateway: "signature verification failed: kid not found". Attaching the raw auth header they sent and gateway log snippet below.

alice-support: repro steps from customer:
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6IjEyMzQ1In0..." \
  -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
2) get 401 with JSON {"error":"signature verification failed: kid not found"}

alice-support: gateway log:
2026-03-12T10:30:12Z gw-1 trace_id=... auth: jwt validation failed: kid=12345 not in current jwks (cache hit)
2026-03-12T10:30:12Z gw-1 trace_id=... response 401

maria-eng: thanks — any pattern on which customer keys are failing? all tokens with kid=12345?

alice-support: yes, all of their tokens include kid 12345. They also said they saw intermittent successes earlier this morning and then it turned into consistent failures.

devon-sre: quick hypothesis: jwks rotated at provider but our JWKS cache still has old set and the new kid isn't present yet. But kid=12345 sounds like an older kid, odd. Do we have evidence the jwks endpoint returned the new key vs old?

kevin-plat: pulled jwks history from cache logs — our JWKS client refreshes every 5m TTL by default. Looking at the request log to the identity provider: 2026-03-12T10:27:00 -> 200 OK, body size 3. No new keys. 10:30:05 -> 200 OK, body size 0 (we return 204?), actually the provider returned 200 with empty body for a short window during rotation. Our jwks loader treated empty body as "no change" and didn't replace cache, so if their kid was recently added then we'd miss it when body empty.

ash-security: hmm. two edge cases to consider here:
- clock skew (nbf/exp) causing other clients to see tokens invalid 
- JWKS caching + provider returning partial/empty responses during rotation -> signature verification errors or kid not found

maria-eng: do we have the raw JWT header/base64? Can someone paste the header so we can confirm kid value and alg?

alice-support: customer pasted this header (decoded): {"alg":"RS256", "kid":"12345"}

devon-sre: ok confirmed. Next step: try an immediate JWKS refresh on gateway (cache purge) and retry request. alice-support, can you trigger a cache purge and have customer retry?

alice-support: done — I hit the admin endpoint to clear jwks cache for that issuer (POST /internal/cache/invalidate?key=issuer:auth.example.com). They retried and got 200 on next request. Customer says it recovered.

ash-security: good repro. Root cause likely provider rotation + transient empty jwks response. We should implement better handling when JWKS body is empty or malformed — treat as transient failure and keep previous keys instead of replacing with empty. Also add logic: on signature errors with "kid not found" trigger background refresh + short cache-bypass for subsequent verification attempts.

kevin-plat: Agreed. Also logging needs to make it clear whether the jwks cache was used vs refreshed. Right now logs say "cache hit" which is ambiguous if the cache contains stale data. Add fields: cache_status=[hit|stale|miss], jwks_etag, jwks_age.

maria-eng: one more wrinkle: customer mentioned they saw other errors last week where tokens were failing with "token not yet valid (nbf)" for a subset of requests. Could be clock skew between our gateway and customer's auth provider. Our JWT library allows a leeway of 5s by default — maybe too tight for their infra.

ash-security: propose we add per-issuer configurable clock_skew_seconds (default 30s) and an env flag to increase global leeway. For immediate mitigation, support increased skew in the gateway config for the FinData tenant.

devon-sre: I'll open a quick patch for two things:
- treat empty JWKS response as transient -> don't overwrite cache, log warning
- on kid-not-found error, trigger an async refresh and mark request to retry once with fresh keys (but don't block request thread)

devon-sre: planning to land as 2-line change in jwks_client.go and a follow-up for cache metrics. Will canary to 10% of gateways first.

kevin-plat: please also include unit tests for scenario: provider returns 200 with empty body, provider returns partial set missing kid, and verify that cache remains unchanged and we retry refresh on kid-not-found.

ash-security: don't forget to consider a malicious provider that serves empty body repeatedly — our backoff logic should cap refresh frequency. We already have exponential backoff, ensure we don't DDoS identity provider.

alice-support: customer asked about long-term mitigation: they can pin key rotation schedule with their IdP and we can add a reconciliation job to fetch jwks every 30s during known rotation windows. Can we offer that as a service?

maria-eng: product question — we could offer "rotation-safe fetch" flag for enterprise customers where we do aggressive polling for 15m post-rotation, but needs opt-in. Add to roadmap.

devon-sre: small followups: what about signature algorithm mismatches? If alg in header != alg in signing key, we should reject upfront. Also log the alg and kid in the 401 response body for support debugging (but avoid leaking public key material).

ash-security: yes, include alg in logs but not in client-facing error messages beyond generic "signature verification failed". For internal support, we can include more detail in the gateway trace logs.

kevin-plat: I'll file GH issue with the three action items and assign:
- JWKS empty-body handling (devon)
- kid-not-found async refresh + retry (devon)
- per-issuer clock_skew config + support doc (maria)

sre-bot: Created issue #1428: "jwks rotation resilience: empty-body, kid-not-found retry, clock skew config" assigned to devon, maria. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/1428 :spiral_notepad:

alice-support: customer updated — they're happy for now. They asked if we can add a short note to support KB about asking customers to try a cache flush (we can provide curl to our admin path) before escalation. I'll draft KB.

maria-eng: thanks everyone. devon please post the PR link here when ready and set DONT_BLOCK tag for canary.

devon-sre: will do, working on tests now. ETA 2 hours.

ash-security: one more test case request: simulate clock skew + jwks partial response together. Sometimes both happen (token nbf + missing kid) and it's tricky to debug. Add integration test in staging harness.

devon-sre: added to test plan.

alice-support: marking this resolved with workaround; will update the support ticket and KB. :thumbsup:
